text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Disputes of the country's top rulers might lead to the postponement of nationwide municipal and mayoral elections, planned for June 1.
-A Palestinian prisoners' rights organisation: Israel is holding four Iranians who were kidnapped in Lebanon.
-The growth of economic activity in Lebanon slowed in January as the central bank's coincident indicator of economic activity fell to 166.0 against 168.3 at the end of December.

-The head of the constitutional court submitted his resignation to protest against political interference in the work of the council which is reviewing appeals lodged by defeated candidates in last summer's parliamentary elections.
-An Eygptian man was executed by hanging for killing a Lebanese man and his wife in 1992.
-Net total public debt rose to 16,433.0 billion pounds in January from 16,138.1 billion at the end of 1996.
-Israeli shelling of Iqlim al-Toufah and Nabatiyeh. A man was wounded in Tuesday's shelling of Nabatiyeh al-Fawqa.
-Employees at public utilities to start an open-ended strike on Saturday.
